title: Data on Jobs Support Scheme Beneficiaries
what_it_is: Data on Jobs Support Scheme Beneficiaries

sections.label: JSS payouts by sector tier
sections.summary: JSS payouts covering October 2019 to April 2020 went to Tier 1, Tier 2 and remaining sectors, benefiting 223,000, 317,000 and 1.7 million employees respectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Sorry, Mr Speaker, I am taking Question Nos 13 and 14 together, with your permission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We do not track the detailed breakdown of the profile of JSS beneficiaries as requested by Assoc Prof Lim.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In terms of industry breakdown, based on the JSS payouts that have been made so far, which cover wages for October 2019 to April 2020, the amount of JSS disbursed to Tier 1 sectors is about $2.2 billion, benefiting 223,000 employees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: For Tier 2 sectors, which comprise arts and culture, marine and offshore, food services, land transport and retail sectors, the total JSS paid out is about $1.9 billion, benefiting 317,000 employees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: For the remaining sectors, the total JSS paid out is about $12.4 billion, benefiting 1.7 million employees.

sections.label: JSS broad-based wage support rationale
sections.summary: The scheme is important for retaining local workforce, and JSS will be reviewed to be more targeted and transit to a Jobs Growth Incentive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: You may not feel the impact of it directly, but I assure you, it is extremely important to have such a scheme to ensure that companies retain their local workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Without such a broad-based wage support scheme, I am quite sure unemployment rates today would be far higher than they are.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We are talking about a period when we had circuit breaker, when a lot of companies were impacted and we had to put in place a broad-based support scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We have already started to differentiate the JSS by tiers and we will continue to review to see how the JSS can be more targeted and transit also now, to a Jobs Growth Incentive, to encourage companies to create new jobs.
